it's the kind of game you play without a break for a while and then just drop it out of the blue, only to come back to it a few months later. The generic checklist gameplay of go to a certain spot and finish certain number of objectives should, on paper, get old really fast. Yet, the game world keeps the locales varied and the enemies interesting enough to mitigate the otherwise dull task of doing ticking things off a checklist on a map that is seemingly as big as IRL Greece itself.

Going into this game blind is perhaps the best way to get the full experience of this game. When you accidentally start a quest chain that leads to amazing views and unbelievable fights, those memories stick with you. It also helps that Kassandra is a compelling character, powered by fantastic voice acting, and a strong personality that makes you want to be her friend.

The game is not without its faults, it can get tedious every now and then, but then all you have to do is go on a sight seeing tour or sail the high seas, and you are ready to resume your journey.

Assassin's Creed Odyssey is a game that has grown on me, and I'd say it's one of my favorites. Initially, I stopped playing due to the repetitive missions, but revisiting it, I found it more engaging this time around. The main story, while not spectacular, sets the stage for the real highlights - the two DLCs, particularly "The Fate of Atlantis".
https://steamcommunity.com/sharedfiles/filedetails/?id=3638162722
The Atlantis DLC is a marvel, introducing new equipment and armors that elevate the gameplay experience. The expansion's focus on exploration and mythological elements adds a fresh layer to the game. The combat, while initially feeling a bit sluggish, has been improved and is now more fluid.
https://steamcommunity.com/sharedfiles/filedetails/?id=3632571480
What truly makes Odyssey stand out is its world and character development. The open-world design, though vast, is filled with meaningful side quests and interactions that breathe life into ancient Greece. The protagonist, Kassandra, is well-developed, and the story's personal touch adds depth to the Assassin's Creed universe.
https://steamcommunity.com/sharedfiles/filedetails/?id=3618206306
Overall, Assassin's Creed Odyssey is a must-play, especially for those who enjoy action-RPGs and open-world exploration. The DLCs, especially Atlantis, are worth experiencing.

I'll get the elephant out of the room...the performance is just awful. Very dissapointing, the engine is really starting to show it's age not to mention the multiple layers of DRM. I really hope this is addressed in the very near future, as it's quite a damp on an otherwise good game.

Moving on-This iteration of Assassin's Creed brings many new gameplay features like conquering areas and their leaders (kinda feels like something out of the middle earth series) as well as an all new dialogue/choice system that has real consequences that will last for the remainder of the game. One of my favourite parts of the new game is the awesome sailing and naval combat, you can upgrade ship and crew in many ways. I don't really like the "romance" system as it's always just some black screen :/

There's lots of RPG skill trees and more to upgrade your character, lot's of different armours and weapons allow deep customisation. Plus you have the choice of male or female character to play.

Despite the performance issues and a couple of bugs I've come across this is a solid open world game that I'm really enjoying, and with all the post launch content planned I may be playing this one for a while to come.

There is no reason this needs to be an Assassins Creed title, but its fun. If you're looking for an ancient Greek themed RPG with lots to do, decent writing, and ok combat, this is the game. Dont expect it to blow you away, but its also not a let down. 7/10

Anyways, I like this game a lot, and recommend it to anyone who likes the sound of the description. I had this games for years, and played well over 100 hours but never complete the whole game. I recently just got the new Samsung 57 inch Neo G9 4K monitor, wanted to play some good open world RPG with the Super Ultrawide. After being completely disappointed that Starfield didn't even support the ultrawide resolution, I came back to this game. Boy, a game that was released 5 years ago, it supports 7680x2160 automatically without any mods, and it just simply look so stunning. The color and visual art style looks better than Starfield's, the shadowing, NPC facial expression, and even the overall environment is 10x better than Starfield. Don't get me wrong, i don't think Starfield is a horrible game, I played well over 40 plus hours. But in comparison to other Triple A open world RPG, its just not nearly as good.

As for AC Odyssey, the story is very interesting, voice acting are great with a nice touch of humor along the way. Its absolutely worth play, especially when the ultimate edition goes on deep discounts.

Gorgeous game, with absolutely PLENTY to do, but it just feels like none of these things matter and Its hard to keep track of what I'm doing and even why. The RPG mechanics are cool but the damage sponge enemies drive me inside, and as someone who loved the original AC trilogy, it's a bummer to see how detached this is from it all.

I've taken multiple 2 - 3 month breaks when playing to just try and get through it, and I'm currently in the middle of my next break, we'll see if I ever pick it up again or actually finish this game.

The haters are triggerad and biased; this game is nothing short of spectacular. Cannot praise the team enough for the sheer scale and complexity of the execution. As a bit of a greek geek I cannot express enough how well they weave real historical locations, figures, and events into the game narrative. The work effort must have been absolutely massive and I feel like it is worth every penny, maybe even more.

As far as the grind claims - Hitting level 33 now and not feeling any of the grind-walls described, nor do I feel any of the bugs. Not seeing a need for DLC or MTX to make the game fun, so not sure what these kids are complaininag about. With that being said, I am so damned impressed with the execution fo this game and how much fun it has been, that I am going to do something I rarely do and actually buy DLC and MTX to support the game even further. The kids are spoiled. Personally, I think these Ubi nailed it and they deserve to be rewarded for the hours I have enjoyed myself.

Odyssey is an amazing game as a separate product that has nothing to do with the original franchise, and if you can only treat it as such, you will be lost in the ancient Greek world which has been designed to awe. I would rate this game highly even only due to the fact the great part of the game was built to reconstruct real-life layouts of the Greek cities and temples, and many pieces of art and statues are 1:1 copies with amazing attention to detail. There are historians publishing their own in-game video tours on YouTube. As a video game, Odyssey is a bit arcadey and won't give you the same experience a Witcher game would or any other more complicated RPG, but if you want to see something beautiful and maybe even learn a lot, if willing, I strongly recommend Assassin's Creed Odyssey.

The last assassins creed I played was AC3 and to be honest I was pretty disappointed with it. At the time I just figured "Huh, I guess this series just isn't for me." and I never tried another AC game. My wife was encouraged to buy this game about a month ago and she did. I watched her play it and it didn't look like the other AC I had played so I bought it as well and gave it a shot.

I'm very glad I did. I haven't been so hooked on a game for a very long time. I've been playing nightly with her and we've had a great time. The world is alive and pretty, I really enjoy the mercenary system, and the quests are plentiful and fun. Moreover climbing is a lot funner than I remember.

Neutral

+/- Tons of weapon types, but daggers are clearly the best

Cons
- Many "points of interest" are just copy and paste caves/camps
- Idiotic animal AI
- Ubisoft went full on RPG in this one (character+equipment stats)
- Level cap is too high at 99
- Gone are the days of sleek parkour introduced in Unity
- Warrior specialization is garbage

PROS:
- Huge, beautiful world to explore both by land and by sea
- V E R Y well optimized
- Fun and engaging combat system that inherently gives the game a lot of replayability
- Funny and interesting side quests
- Interesting main story
- Choice of Female or Male protagonist
- Ability to get it on with guys or gals

CONS:
- The low amount of XP gained from completing quests clearly emphasizes buying the XP boost available from the in-game store for $10
-^ S e r i o u s l y??? Micro-transactions in a single-player game? This is kinda unheard of.
- Very few interesting cutscenes. Almost all conversation scenes are shot-reverse-shot and very boring to watch, which leads to getting less invested in the characters,
- Excluding a couple of chapter-ending moments, your choices really don't matter all that much and will not impact the story beyond the next line of dialogue,
- The open world is wide but shallow, offering a lot of repeat activities to hit 100%

If you want to take it slow, the filler is still bad, mainly fetch quests. Still, I encourage exploring ancient Greece.

If you're a fan of this new open-world direction that the AC games are taking (I am) then you'll definitely have a great time. The open world is really beautifully designed, exploring ancient Greek cities is fascinating, and the controls are usually snappy and responsive. The gameplay moves quickly, unlike other games in the Open-world RPG genre.

People tend to swear that one protagonist (Alexios vs Kassandra) is the 'superior' choice. That's obviously nonsense, as the existence of the argument just proves how well-acted and scripted both characters are.

My next one will actually be AC3, so going back to the old style. I missed that game when I came out, and I'd like to go back for it before Valhalla. That said, I'm by no means done with Odyssey, as there are really 3 major plot threads to follow, and resolving the 'main' story is just one of those pieces.

This game has a ridiculous amount of content. Quests, gear, abilities, mastery points, locations, conquest battles, ship battles, levels, armor set bonuses, mercenaries, cultists, sex partners, islands, historical sites, bounty quests, weekly quests, special currency, DLC cultists, DLC quests.

It is genuinely too much, but I've never had a game feel as complete.

This is one of the best role-playing games I've ever played. And I know its not a traditional RPG in that sense, but it really does cast you into the role of a Greek hero and gives you an incredible sense of immersion into this ancient world. Top marks for that.

The graphics, sound effects, music, voice acting and gameplay are all superb. Very fun game to just wander around exploring and fighting and looting. You will massacre a shitload of people in this game and acquire vast riches. The naval combat is also really fun.

Get it, you will love this!
It's a bootleg witcher 3 plagued by a grating story and infuriating level based combat that turns what would be satisfying stealth kills and sword slices to long health bar tomfoolery.

The most depressing thing that I found on this game is that you completely don't have a side? It really doesn't make any sense. You could clear every fort for one team and they would still see you as an enemy, or sometimes you would walk into the enemy fort that you haven't touched once and they would see you as an ally, like wtf?

Also the system that revives the enemy heroes and the bounty hunters doesn't really make much sense, you kill them and next time you login they're just there again.

You clear a fort fully? Oh, great! good job! it will spawn as an enemy fort as soon as you move a bit further away...? They seriously didn't put much thought into it.

TLTR: This game doesn't really progress map-wise and you will clear the same stuff over and over and over...

Don't take me wrong I still recommend the game because it's awesome but like.. yea, this stuff could've been avoided if you would have 1 or 2 braincells working.

Great game, this is my second open world game after breath of the wild and I absolutely loved it. The story is fun, great characters and very dynamic with the choices you can make.
It is worth mention that the travelling around is suuuper annoying, at first I was marvelled by the beauty of the scenery of Greece and the fun missions you can do all around. But after 20-30 hours of play it starts to become very tedious having to travel very far (the map is huge), despite the quick travel, for a simple and quite repetitive mission, specially when you are inside towns where you move even slower or the damn horse doesn't even want to run. In the end I ran through the main story just to finish it, didn't even finished exploring the entire map.
Still definitely recommend the game, it is a great game that could have been even better either being smaller or with better travelling mechanics. If you love exploring and maybe learn a little bit about ancient Greece history you should play it.

tldr.text: Very Positive (89%): players love the story and characters, cited in 59% of reviews.
The story and characters also draw the most complaints, so opinion on the story is split.

details.text: Recent reviews complain less often about the story and about bugs and crashes than they did before.
New players who reviewed within their first two hours are mostly unimpressed, at 40% positive, while veterans with over 50 hours give 93%.
